producer_checks.information_cutoff: 19 Nov 2026 16:00 BRT / 19:00 UTC. The IEA World Energy Outlook 2026 is dated 19 Nov; exact public release hour is not stated, but its page was available by cutoff. Reuters's US market report was first published 18 Nov at 10:28 UTC and updated on 19 Nov; the final figures in the current version are used. US equity closes refer to 18 Nov because the 19 Nov session had not closed. The Reuters 09:53 GMT oil quote is intraday. The Edge Asian closing edition was first published at 11:08 GMT on 19 Nov.
producer_checks.novelty: Compared with 16 Nov (China/Japan activity and dollar funding), 17 Nov (semiconductor repricing and Brazil activity/inflation expectations), and 18 Nov (European inflation and AI financing), this edition uses the newly dated IEA World Energy Outlook 2026 to quantify energy-security capital requirements: bypass pipeline scenarios, grid kilometres, equipment bottlenecks, importer investment and emerging-market financing constraints. It does not repeat the previous edition's AI-contract analysis.
producer_checks.evidence_vintage: IEA WEO 2026 is a scenario report dated 19 Nov, not a realised project pipeline. IEA Oil Market Report is dated 13 Nov. EIA petroleum stocks refer to the week ended 13 Nov and report released 18 Nov. Treasury curve, US equity closes, FX and gold observations refer to 18 Nov; Reuters's final US index values are taken from the current version of its market report, first published 18 Nov at 10:28 UTC and updated on 19 Nov. The 19 Nov Brent/WTI quote is a Reuters wire observation at 09:53 GMT reproduced by Media Selangor. Asian equity data are 19 Nov closing returns in The Edge edition first published at 11:08 GMT. Eurostat October HICP is a final release published 18 Nov. World Bank debt figures refer to 2025.
producer_checks.bilingual_parity: EN and PT-BR use the same 14 source URLs, 18 Nov settlement values, 19 Nov 09:53 GMT oil quote, final US equity returns, semiconductor index direction, Asian closing returns and qualifications. The source vintages and cutoff are aligned.
producer_checks.visual_evidence: Two explicit bar charts, three evidence tables, one regional map and one causal flow. Existing chart values are unchanged; the revised market table and Asian closing paragraph match across EN/PT-BR. Scenarios remain uncharted as observations.
producer_checks.source_limitations: No harmonised same-date global private credit-spread series, project-finance margins, delivered diesel prices or verified project-level grid capex/disbursements were established. The 19 Nov oil quote is an intraday Reuters wire observation reproduced by Media Selangor, not a close. The Edge's Asian closing percentages are its calculations from exchange/administrator closing data; its page does not establish a single cause for Taiwan's decline.

limitations: The exact publication hour of the IEA World Energy Outlook 2026 is not stated on its 19 November page.
IEA scenarios and system requirements are modelled pathways, not realised infrastructure, committed capital or guaranteed policy outcomes.
The 7 mb/d pipeline figure includes projects under construction or consideration; the Low Hormuz Case depends on multiple conditional assumptions.
US EIA inventories are a national weekly observation and cannot establish global diesel availability.
Treasury par yields do not measure private credit spreads, project-finance margins or sovereign borrowing spreads.
The Asian equity figures are closing returns from The Edge's 19 November closing edition, first published at 11:08 GMT; they are not the earlier 03:51 GMT intraday snapshot.
The World Bank debt aggregates are not energy-project debt and do not identify the financing terms of individual infrastructure projects.
The Brazil market move reflects domestic fiscal uncertainty as well as external dollar and rate conditions.
The 19 November Brent/WTI quote at 09:53 GMT is an intraday observation from a Reuters wire reproduced by Media Selangor, not a settlement.
contrary_evidence: Brent and WTI fell on 18 November and US commercial crude inventories rose in the week ended 13 November, consistent with a looser near-term crude balance.
The IEA expects oil supply to rebound in 2027, which could lower benchmark prices if the forecast materialises.
India's rupee remained resilient despite a stronger dollar, with reported November equity inflows supporting the currency.
US crude and distillate inventories increased in the latest weekly EIA balance, even while the IEA describes low global on-land stocks and tight diesel markets.
The IEA's grid and pipeline figures are system requirements and scenario assumptions, not proof of project bankability or implementation.

en.title: Global Macro — Energy security turns the Hormuz shock into a global capital-allocation test
en.deck: The IEA's new outlook quantifies the capital, equipment and financing needed to diversify energy supply and expand electricity grids, even as crude prices soften.
en.regime: Energy-security repricing and accelerated electrification under elevated dollar rates and uneven access to long-duration capital.
en.key_risk: Lower crude prices may ease near-term inflation without resolving grid, equipment, route and financing constraints that determine delivered energy reliability.
